### Investment Memo: AKAM — November 10, 2026

**Verdict**: SELL | Conviction: Medium (High on fundamentals, Low on price path)
**Price Target**: $55 (-31% from current $80.29) | Base-case range $45–65; acknowledged tail outcomes $25–$138
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

---

**Investment Thesis**

Akamai has converted itself from a cash-generative, narrow-moat CDN/security franchise into a **junk-rated (BB+), negative-free-cash-flow, single-counterparty AI datacenter landlord**. The $11.6B, seven-year Anthropic contract — funded with ~$5.5B of debt-financed capex and a 5% equity warrant at admittedly the *lowest-return pricing in the book* (~15% ROIC) — arrives just as legacy delivery shrinks 3–7%/yr, gross margin has collapsed ~900bps since 2021, and ROIC (5.3%) sits below WACC for a third straight year. There is no fraud here (Beneish −2.80, accruals −0.093, cash conversion 3.4x) — this is a capital-allocation and business-model problem. At $80, the market is capitalizing low-margin hosting revenue as software; intrinsic value on SBC-expensed economics is ~$55. The honest offset: $14B of *signed* commitments against an $11.6B market cap means the option is nearly free — but you cannot size a position on one customer, no FCF, and a negative Kelly.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Neutral. ~80% of AKAM's risk is idiosyncratic, 20% macro (strong USD −1pt on the 50% international book; 5.13% 10Y caps the multiple at ~12x). The CDN/edge/security sector is bifurcated: security and AI-inference grow 11–23%, legacy delivery is commoditizing. AKAM is the **slowest grower (−9.1pp vs peer median) and lowest-gross-margin name (−24.1pp)** in its true competitive set, albeit one of only three GAAP-profitable. Bull scenario: fast disinflation → $100–110 on multiple alone.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: **Medium.** Clean litigation, no Russia/China, no country ≥10% of revenue. The risk is direction of travel: EU CADA sovereignty rules targeting non-EU cloud providers, export-control dependencies on the Anthropic build, and an unexecuted **Data Processing Addendum on the $11.6B MSA** (GDPR/CCPA exposure — escalated by two independent agents).
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: **SELL.** Moat narrow and narrowing; ROIC 5.3% < WACC; SBC $526M exceeds GAAP net income; ~$4B of buybacks at $90–130 destroyed; net debt ~$7.4–8.3B pro forma. DCF base ≈ **$55**; bull ≈ $138. The spread is an admission the business is now underwritable only as an option.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: **HOLD.** The inflection is real: CIS bookings $2.8B → >$14B in one quarter, 2027 guide +17–22%, >$7B revenue by 2028. But guidance has been cut twice in two quarters, 2027 EPS is *flat* while D&A and interest rise, and FY26 FCF ≈ **−$2.0B**. Growth is being bought with capital, not earned with margin.
- **Quantitative Signals**: **Neutral, tilt Sell.** #1 of 3 on value (13x EV/EBITDA), #3 on momentum (−11.8%) and quality — the empirical signature of a **value trap**. Realised vol 68%, beta 1.49, max drawdown −52%, R² ~0.10 (90% idiosyncratic — beta-based sizing fails here). The "+17% revision upgrade" flag is a calculation artifact; true broker revision direction is negative.
- **Financial Risk**: **HIGH.** Net debt/EBITDA 4.3x → **6.7x** in nine months; gross debt $9.45B; Altman Z ~1.17–1.71 (distress boundary); **lenders cut the secured basket from 10% to 3.5% of assets**; FY26E FCF −$2.0B (forward FCF yield ≈ −17%); $1.15B of converts due 2027 settle in cash at $80 spot. A −20% revenue scenario eliminates EBIT entirely and pushes leverage toward 18–20x.
- **Non-Financial Risk**: **HIGH.** Not integrity — independence, no enforcement, independent chair — but stacked vectors: existential counterparty concentration, execution risk with documented slippage ($30M already slipped Q4→2027; only ~70% of hardware procured), **12 insider sales / ~$8.2M and zero open-market buys through a 53% drawdown**, and no succession plan for a 69-year-old founder-CEO mid-way through the largest capital program in company history.
- **ESG**: **Average, negative momentum.** Best-in-class disclosure (externally assured, first exchange-executed VPPA) but decarbonisation running backwards: intensity +37%, clean-energy share −7pp, PUE 1.40 → 1.48, 2030 target progress regressing 47% → 42% — just as the energy bill for the Anthropic build lands. Neutral to the thesis, but an under-priced cost-of-capital risk on a newly junk-rated issuer.
- **Alternative Data**: **Neutral, leaning bearish.** Google Trends −32% QoQ, Stocktwits mentions −67% — the *narrative* has fully unwound while the *contracts* remain intact. Revenue surprises compressed to ±0.8%; the market has stopped paying for beats (Q3 beat → −9.4%). Alt data does not corroborate the +9.6% YoY acceleration consensus needs in Q4.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: **SHORT (not Strong).** Deterioration is already in the cash flow statement, not a forecast. Withheld "Strong" because there is no fraud catalyst, $3.5B cash remains, and a stock with 25 moves >5% in a year can carry a short out on a stretcher.

---

**Bull Case**
1. **$14B signed book vs $11.6B market cap.** If Anthropic performs and pricing improves on follow-on contracts, 2028 revenue >$7B at ~30% non-GAAP margins → ~$9.50–10 EPS → $145–150 at 15x (+80%).
2. **Security is a real franchise.** $2.4B+, +10%, high switching costs — a SOTP case exists if the legacy delivery drag is ever excised.
3. **Macro asymmetry.** A fast disinflation re-rates the multiple ~25% on an unchanged story; beta 0.66 long-run, and positioning is capitulation-level washed out.

**Bear Case**
1. **The economics don't work at spot.** IV ~$55 with SBC expensed and Anthropic at cost of capital; FY26–27 cumulative funding gap ~$2.8B on top of ~$8.3B net debt; D&A cliff hits GAAP EPS precisely when credibility is needed most.
2. **One counterparty is the entire growth story.** Anthropic is private, cash-consuming, non-exclusive, with hyperscaler alternatives; a deferral strands $5.5B of purpose-built, rapidly-obsolescing assets against $9.5B of debt.
3. **Financing is now reflexive.** BB+ with negative outlook, covenant baskets already tightened, equity at $80 — a further raise is either expensive debt or dilutive equity, and both re-price the stock down.

**Key Risks**
- **Anthropic deferral/renegotiation** — the single event that invalidates 2027–28 models (probability: medium, impact: severe)
- **Q4'26 print (Feb 18, 2027)**: capex must land inside $3.46–3.66B with no new raise; a miss is a binary negative
- **Second downgrade / further covenant tightening**; 2027 convert maturity settling in cash
- **Gross margin below 53%** — no floor confirmed; CIS decelerating (+39% → +35%) before the ramp
- **EU CADA / export controls** constraining siting of contracted capacity

**Portfolio Construction Note**
**PASS — 0% at $80.29.** Kelly fraction is *negative* at spot (25% bull $145 / 45% grind $85 / 30% bear $55 → f* ≈ −0.05). At 68% vol and 1.49 beta, even 1% consumes ~0.6x the risk budget of a normal 2% tech position, and AKAM is functionally a **short-credit-spread instrument in equity clothing** — it doubles any existing AI-capex/leveraged-infra exposure while tilting the book into the negative-momentum/negative-quality factor corner. Pre-committed ladder: **1.5% at ≤$65** with Q4'26 capex in guidance and no equity raise; **2.5–3%** adding CIS ≥$275M/qtr and GM ≥54%; **1.0–1.5% even at $85–95** if the Feb 18, 2027 print delivers proof. Hard invalidation: Anthropic deferral, equity issuance, capex outside guidance, GM <53%, Security <+5%, second downgrade. If neither price nor proof triggers by Q1 2028, close the watchlist. **Patience is the position.**

---

**Data gaps & integrity flags**: EV is contested ($16–20B; we use ~$19–20B including Nov converts); convertible issuance amounts are inconsistently reported across sources ($2.2B/$2.6B/$3.5B — confirm vs 10-K); no peer valuation multiples exist in the toolkit (FMP sector endpoint returns mega-caps only); Sortino, CDS, and full debt ladder unavailable; 10-K/DEF 14A full text returned 403s (chair/CEO separation unconfirmed); one quant risk module is internally inconsistent with raw prices. Agents agree on facts; disagreement on price implication is noted and resolved toward the SBC-expensed base case.

# AKAM — Portfolio Construction Recommendation

**Verified reference data (Nov 9, 2026 close): $80.29.** Market cap ~$11.6B (144.2M sh). 52-wk range **$77.37–$165.45** (high May 13, 2026). Realised 252d vol **68.3%**, beta vs SPY **1.49**, max drawdown **51.7%**, Sharpe **−0.02**, 12-1 momentum **−11.75%**. I re-verified the price series directly — the Short Analyst's ~$122 quote is stale (that was the Sep 25 level) and the Quant Analyst's "re-based 37% vol" is wrong; the raw OHLC series (eight >10% single-day moves in 12 months, incl. +26.6% on 5/8 and −16.7% on 4/10) confirms the 68%/52% figures. **Every conclusion below uses $80.29.**

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary Table

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Value** | Sell / Avoid | **High** | IV $45–65 (base $55) vs $80.29. ROIC 5.3% < WACC for 3 straight yrs. SBC $526M > net income. ~$4B of buybacks destroyed. |
| **Fin Risk** | High risk | **High** | Net debt/EBITDA 4.26x → **6.70x**; FY26E FCF **−$2.0B**; Altman Z 1.71 (distress boundary); lender cut secured basket 10%→3.5%. |
| **Non-Fin Risk** | High risk | Med-High | Single-counterparty concentration; **zero insider buys through a 53% drawdown**; Anthropic MSA DPA unexecuted at signing; no CEO succession. |
| **Short** | Short (not strong) | Medium | **No fraud** (Beneish −2.80, accruals −0.093). Business-model/capital-allocation problem. *Uses stale $122 price — bear case overstated relative to spot.* |
| **Growth** | Hold | Med-High | $14B signed CIS book vs $11.6B cap; **+80% bull / −30% bear**. Needs Q4'26 capex landing + CIS ≥$275M/qtr to become Buy. |
| **Quant** | Neutral, tilt Sell | Medium | "Cheap and broken." #1 of 3 on value (13x EV/EBITDA), **#3 on momentum and quality**. Value-trap signature. |
| **Sector** | Neutral | Medium | Slowest grower (−9.1pp vs peer median) and lowest GM (−24.1pp) in the competitive set, though one of few GAAP-profitable. |
| **Geo/Legal** | Medium risk | Medium | Clean litigation, no Russia/China, no country >10%. Risk is *direction of travel*: EU CADA, BB+ downgrade, $11.6B single counterparty + 5% warrant. |
| **Macro** | Neutral (mild −) | Medium | ~**80% idiosyncratic**, 20% macro. FX −3.2% USD, 5.13% 10Y caps multiple. Bull = disinflation → $100–110. |
| **Alt Data** | Neutral/bearish | Medium | Trends −32% QoQ, Stocktwits −67%; contracts intact but *narrative has fully unwound*. Market stopped paying for beats (Q3 beat, −9.4%). |
| **ESG** | Average, neg. momentum | Low-Med | Carbon intensity **+37%**, clean-energy share −7pp, PUE 1.48 → 2030 target regressing 47%→42%. Neutral to the thesis. |
| **Sector/Consensus** | **Split** | — | Unanimous on *facts*; split on *price implication*. |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment: **SPLIT** — but the split is shallower than it looks

**High agreement on the facts (10 of 11 agents):** gross margin 63.3%→54.7%; ROIC 9.0%→5.3%; FCF +$699M (FY25) → **−$2.0B (FY26E)**; net debt ~$8.3B; S&P **BB+**; SBC ~12% of revenue; delivery shrinking 3–7%/yr; the growth plan rests on one counterparty.

**The genuine disagreement is narrow and resolvable:**
- *Bear camp* (Value, Short, Fin Risk, Quant): the deterioration is structural and the price still doesn't discount it.
- *Bull camp* (Growth, Macro bull scenario, Alt Data's "contracts intact"): the market assigns ~zero value to a $14B signed book; 3.6x EV/2027E revenue is an option, not a valuation.

**Conflict resolutions I am imposing:**
1. **Value over Growth on intrinsic value.** Growth's $145 requires *both* flawless execution *and* a 15x re-rating. Value's $55 base expenses SBC and prices Anthropic at cost of capital — management itself concedes this deal carries the **lowest-return pricing in the book (~15% ROIC)**. The default valuation is Value's; Growth's number is the option payoff, not the base case.
2. **Short Analyst down-weighted on price.** Its bear multiple math (37x FCF, 108x owner earnings) was struck at $122. At $80.29 EV is ~$19–20B, i.e. **~28x FY25 FCF and ~83x owner earnings** — still unacceptable, but roughly 30% of the bear case has *already been paid out*. This is the single biggest correction in the file.
3. **Quant's risk statistics corrected upward, not downward.** 68% vol / 1.49 beta / 52% drawdown are real. This *tightens* sizing.
4. **Macro deferred.** A disinflation-driven multiple re-rating is a market call, not an AKAM edge. We do not size a single-name position on a Fed forecast.
5. **Non-Fin Risk's DPA finding escalated.** An $11.6B AI-workload MSA effective with privacy terms *still to be negotiated* is a live GDPR/CCPA and enterprise-contract exposure that no agent elsewhere flagged.

**Net: conviction on the fundamentals is HIGH and bearish; conviction on the price path is LOW. Under the framework, that combination is a sizing problem, not a buy signal.**

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation: **0% — PASS at $80.29**

**Kelly check (base-case probabilities: 25% bull $145 / 45% grind ~$85 / 30% bear $55):**
- At **$80.29**: EV = 0.25(+81%) + 0.45(+6%) + 0.30(−32%) = **+8.5%**, with 68% vol and a 2.4:1 payoff. Kelly f* = (pb−q)/b = (0.25×2.53 − 0.75)/2.53 = **−0.05 → negative. Zero allocation.**
- At **$65**: EV = 0.25(+123%) + 0.45(+31%) + 0.30(−15%) = **+40%**; Kelly f* ≈ 0.16 → quarter-Kelly ≈ **4%**. Full 2–3% starter justified.

**Therefore the sizing ladder is price-and-proof conditional:**

| Condition | Position |
|---|---|
| **Today, $80.29** | **0%** |
| Mandate *requires* AI-infra/AKAM tracking exposure | **0.25–0.50%** maximum, hard-stopped, treated as a tracking position not an investment |
| Price ≤ **$65** *with* Q4'26 capex inside guidance and no new equity raise | **1.5%** |
| Price ≤ $65 **and** CIS ≥$275M in a quarter **and** GM stabilised ≥54% | **2.5–3.0%** |
| Price ≤ $55 (base-case IV) with credit outlook stable | **3.5–4.0%** |
| Q4'26 (Feb 18, 2027) delivers capex ≤$3.66B, CIS on track, margin trough confirmed | **1.0–1.5%** even at $85–95 — pay up for de-risked evidence, not for narrative |

**Why not even a small position now:** the sizing framework says "low conviction or multiple risk flags → 0.5–1% or pass." AKAM has **four independent HIGH-risk ratings** (Financial, Non-Financial, credit, and 68% realised vol). At a 68% vol / 1.49 beta, a 1% position contributes **0.68% of standalone portfolio volatility** and roughly **0.6x the risk budget of a 2% position in a normal 35%-vol tech name**. Limited partners are not paid for a 0.25% position in a junk-rated single-counterparty capex vehicle; the research cost is sunk either way, and optionality is better acquired *after* the Feb 2027 print when the binary resolves.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

**Measured correlations (252d, verified):** SPY **0.31** · XLK **0.42** · MSFT **0.16** · NET **0.29** · FSLY **0.55**.

- **Sector concentration:** *Neutral-to-positive.* AKAM is Technology, but its 0.42 correlation to XLK and 0.16 to MSFT mean it is **not redundant tech beta**. It would not materially increase a book's effective tech factor exposure.
- **Correlation:** *Positive.* Lowest-correlation positioning in a year where R² vs SPY is only ~0.10 — ~90% idiosyncratic. Genuine diversification of *return source*.
- **Factor exposure:** *Negative.* AKAM loads **positively on value** (13x EV/EBITDA, #1 in peer set) and **deeply negatively on momentum (−11.75%, #3 of 3) and quality (ROIC 5.3%, #3 of 3)**. Adding it tilts the book toward "cheap and deteriorating." If the portfolio already holds value/contrarian or cyclical-recovery names, this **compounds an existing factor bet** — the highest-risk form of concentration.
- **Hidden factor: it is a credit instrument in equity clothing.** ~$9.5–11B gross debt, BB+, negative FCF, one counterparty. With IG OAS at **93bp** (tight: 74bp in June), AKAM is a **short-volatility/short-credit-spread position**. Credit widening hits it far harder than equity beta implies. Any portfolio already carrying AI-capex or leveraged-infrastructure exposure is doubling that bet.
- **Liquidity:** ~1.5M sh/day, ~$130M notional — no capacity constraint, but note the *exit* liquidity is asymmetric: 16.2M shares traded on Nov 9 (10x normal) on a −3% day.

**Verdict: acceptable diversifier on correlation alone; unacceptable on factor and credit-fit given it adds a leveraged AI-capex bet with negative momentum and negative quality at a price with no margin of safety.**

---

## 5. Entry Strategy: **Scale-in only — never all at once**

The stock has eight >10% single-day moves in twelve months and gapped −9.4% on a *beat*. Market-order execution is a donation. **Do not initiate at $80.29.** The pre-committed plan:

- **Tranche 1 (0.75%):** only at **≤$65** *or* after Feb 18, 2027 if capex lands ≤$3.66B AND no equity raise AND CIS ≥$275M annualised run-rate.
- **Tranche 2 (0.75–1.0%):** GM stabilises ≥54% for two consecutive quarters with CIS still ≥30% growth.
- **Tranche 3 (1.0%):** credit stabilises — outlook revised from negative, or net debt/EBITDA <5.0x.
- Use limit orders across 3–5 sessions; avoid the two weeks bracketing an earnings date.
- **If neither the price nor the proof condition triggers by Q1 2028, close the watchlist item.** Do not let a "potential" position drift into a narrative holding.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Hard stop (price):** closing basis **$68.00** — ~15% below spot and just under the 12-month closing low of $71.97. Given 4.3% daily σ, intraday stops are noise; use weekly closes.

**Thesis invalidation (any one → exit regardless of price):**
1. **Q4'26 capex outside $3.46–3.66B, or any equity/common issuance** (converts at distressed terms count).
2. **Any Anthropic deferral, capacity re-pricing, or renegotiation disclosure** — this alone is ~100% of the growth story and the ~$5.5B of purpose-built capex.
3. **CIS revenue below $250M in any quarter of 2027** (vs the $275–325M/qtr needed for the $1.1–1.3B guide).
4. **Second downgrade (B+ or below) or a further secured-basket cut.**
5. **Gross margin below 53%** — the floor has not yet been found and this is the cleanest read on whether the pivot is margin-dilutive or margin-accretive.
6. **Security revenue growth below +5%** — the last durable franchise funding the build.

**Trim trigger:** reduce by half at **$110** and exit entirely at **$120–130**. That band is ~11x 2029 bull-case EBITDA and 2.2–2.4x base-case IV. On a name we cannot underwrite, capture the option value rather than riding a narrative we don't believe.

**Monitoring (quarterly):** net debt/EBITDA (currently 6.70x, target <5.0x); FCF (currently −$2.0B annualising); the unexecuted Anthropic DPA; any insider open-market **purchase** (zero in 12 months, 12 sales ~$8.2M — a single CFO or CEO buy through this drawdown would be a genuine signal).

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **PASS**

**No position at $80.29.** Place AKAM on the watchlist with a pre-committed, written entry ladder at **≤$65 or post-Q4'26 proof**, and a hard invalidation checklist.

**The one-paragraph case:** AKAM is a narrow-moat, formerly asset-light CDN/security business that has become a **junk-rated (BB+), negative-free-cash-flow, single-counterparty AI datacenter landlord** — funded with $5.5B of debt and a 5% equity warrant — while its legacy delivery business shrinks 3–7% a year and ROIC (5.3%) sits below its cost of capital for a third consecutive year. That is a genuine business-model problem, not a fraud, and markets can tolerate those far longer than the bears expect. The offsetting truth is equally real: **$14B of signed contractual commitments against an $11.6B market cap and 3.6x 2027E revenue means the market is paying almost nothing for the option**, and a fast disinflation could re-rate the multiple 25% on an unchanged fundamental story. But you cannot size a position on a macro call for a company with one customer, no free cash flow, and three downgrades — and at $80.29 the Kelly arithmetic is *negative*. The asymmetry becomes payable at $65, and the proof arrives on **February 18, 2027**. We wait for one or the other. **Patience is the position; capital is preserved for the point where conviction and price agree.**

---

**Data gaps to disclose in the memo:** (1) Net debt/EV is contested across agents — $8.30B net debt (Q3'26) vs Growth's $16–17B EV and Quant's $17.5B EV; I use **~$19–20B EV** to include the Nov 2026 converts, and flag a $16–20B range. (2) Convertible issuance is reported inconsistently ($2.2B Nov 2026 vs $3.5B May 2026 vs $2.6B upsized) — confirm against the 10-K. (3) No peer valuation multiples exist in the toolkit (FMP sector endpoint returned mega-caps only), so all relative-value work is peer-median growth/margin construction, not multiples. (4) Sortino, CDS spreads, and full debt-maturity ladder unavailable. (5) 10-K risk factors and DEF 14A text returned 403s across three agents; chair/CEO separation is unconfirmed.

## SECTOR BRIEF: AKAM (Akamai Technologies)

**Sector:** Technology — Software/Internet Infrastructure (CDN, Edge Compute, Application Security)
**Note on peer selection:** FMP's "Technology" sector list is dominated by mega-caps (AAPL, NVDA, MSFT), which are not meaningful comps. I benchmarked against the true competitive set — CDN/edge/application-security vendors — pulled directly.

---

### 1. Sector Overview

Akamai sits at the intersection of two markets with opposite economics. Global CDN is a **~$32.7bn (2025) → $38.8bn (2026) market growing ~11–12% CAGR**, but growth is concentrated in security and edge compute while core media/content delivery is commoditising under hyperscaler price pressure (CloudFront, Azure Front Door, Google Cloud CDN) — Akamai's own delivery revenue fell ~5% in 2025 and ~7% YoY in Q1 2026. Edge computing (broad definitions $70bn–$260bn, 13–23% CAGR) and AI inference-at-edge are the growth vector, but require heavy distributed capex and are being contested by neoclouds and hyperscalers with far deeper balance sheets. The sector is therefore **bifurcated: a mature, deflating legacy delivery layer bolted to an early-growth, capital-hungry edge/AI layer** — and every incumbent (AKAM, FSLY, FFIV) is racing to re-mix revenue before delivery erosion outruns the new growth.

---

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **AI inference demand is landing at the edge.** Akamai signed an **$11.6bn Anthropic AI cloud deal** and **>$14bn of multiyear customer commitments in 2026**; Cloud Infrastructure Services revenue grew **+34% YoY to $109m in Q3 2026**, with management guiding that segment to **$1.1–1.3bn in 2027** and total company revenue growth of **17–22%** — a step-change from 5.4% in FY25.
- **Security is a structurally growing, high-retention attach.** Security revenue reached **$2.24bn (+10%)**, now >50% of Akamai's mix; managed CDN security services is a ~$5.1bn (2026) market compounding high-single digits, with strong switching costs from WAF/bot/DDoS embedded in the traffic path.
- **Distributed footprint is a scarce asset.** ~4,100 PoPs embedded inside 1,300+ carrier networks is expensive to replicate and increasingly relevant for low-latency inference and sovereignty-sensitive workloads — a genuine barrier to entry.

---

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **Delivery price deflation is structural, not cyclical.** Media/content delivery is a near-pure commodity; hyperscalers bundle CDN free into cloud commitments. Akamai's delivery line is shrinking ~5–7% annually, and the segment still carries much of the installed base and gross profit.
- **Capex intensity is crushing margins.** Gross margin has fallen **64.6% (FY20) → 54.7% (FY25)**, ~-10pp, and operating margin **20.6% → 14.9%**, as colocation/egress and D&A (now **$709m, 16.8% of revenue**, up 24% since 2023) scale with cloud infrastructure. AKAM is raising **$2.2bn of convertible notes (Nov 2026)** to fund build-out — leverage and execution risk rising.
- **Share loss in the growth narrative.** Cloudflare is winning developer-led edge/security share with a 75%+ gross margin model, and the AI-cloud pivot pits Akamai against neoclouds and hyperscalers with lower cost of capital. Supply-chain/data-centre delays already pushed revenue out of Q4 2026.

---

### 4. Peer Comparison Table (latest fiscal year)

| Company | Rev ($m) | Rev growth | Gross margin | Operating margin | Net margin | Profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AKAM** (FY25, Dec) | 4,208 | **+5.4%** | **54.7%** | **14.9%** | 10.7% | CDN → security/AI cloud |
| FTNT (FY25, Dec) | 6,800 | +14.2% | 80.8% | 30.6% | 27.3% | Network security |
| FFIV (FY26, Sep) | 3,417 | +10.6% | 82.2% | 23.9% | 21.1% | ADC / app delivery |
| ZS (FY26, Jul) | 3,353 | +25.4% | 76.8% | -4.0% | -1.9% | Cloud security (SASE) |
| NET (FY25, Dec) | 2,168 | **+29.8%** | 74.5% | -9.6% | -4.7% | Edge / security |
| FSLY (FY25, Dec) | 624 | +14.8% | 57.1% | -18.9% | -19.5% | Pure-play CDN |
| RDWR (FY25, Dec) | 302 | +9.8% | 80.7% | 3.8% | 6.7% | App delivery/security |
| **Peer median** | — | **+14.5%** | **78.8%** | **-0.1%** | — | — |
| **AKAM vs median** | — | **-9.1pp** | **-24.1pp** | **+15.0pp** | — | — |

*Growth/margins computed from reported income statements. Note: FMP's sector-aggregate endpoint returned unusable data (company_count=1 per period), so the sector median above is my own construction from the competitive set — the honest benchmark.*

**Read-through:** AKAM is the **slowest grower and lowest-gross-margin name in the group**, but also one of only two with genuinely positive operating margins (the other being FTNT and FFIV). It is a profitable incumbent losing relative growth — the classic "value trap vs. re-rating" setup. FSLY, the closest pure-play comp, is both slower-growing *and* structurally unprofitable, which frames the bear case for pure CDN economics.

---
